findings.location: <article> second paragraph (source.html): "She had spent a week with her aunt and uncle..."
findings.source_quote: She had spent a week with her aunt and uncle who lived several counties over from hers and while there, her cousin Paul had given her a knife that he had made.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate "aunt and uncle" correctly as "shangazi na mjomba" (or another correct Kiswahili pair) and keep the rest of the sentence meaning intact. For example: "Alikuwa ametembelea shangazi na mjomba wake waliokaa wilayani nyingine kwa wiki moja, na wakati huo binamu wake Paul alimpa kisu aliyemutengenezea."
findings.translation_quote: Alikuwa ametembelea shangazi na shangazi yake waliokaa wilayani nyingine kwa wiki moja na wakati huo, binamu wake Paul alimpa kisu alichotengeneza.

findings.location: <article> paragraph describing the injury (source.html): "Just as she landed, her ankle turned and gave way under her. She fell awkwardly onto her left leg."
findings.source_quote: Just as she landed, her ankle turned and gave way under her. She fell awkwardly onto her left leg.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the body part: translate "ankle" as "kiwiko cha mguu wa chini (kiuno cha mguu?)" or better "kiwiko cha mguu" or "mkwaju" (common Kiswahili for ankle). Suggested Kiswahili: "Wakati alipotua, kifundo cha mguu wake kiligeuka na kumkaba. Alianguka kwa mgongo kwa mguu wake wa kushoto." (Keep meaning that the ankle twisted and she fell awkwardly onto her left leg.)
findings.translation_quote: Wakati alipoanguka, kiuno chake kiligeuka na kukata chini. Alianguka kwa namna ya kukosa mkao kwenye mguu wa kushoto.

findings.location: <article> paragraph on God protecting her (source.html): "she is grateful that God protected her"
findings.source_quote: Even though she acted foolishly, she is grateful that God protected her, but she still wishes she had confessed her disobedience to her mother.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the verb "protected" faithfully. The Kiswahili must convey that God protected/saved her (e.g., "alimtegemea" is incorrect). Use "alimtetea" or "almulinda". Suggested revision: "Ingawa alitenda kwa ujinga, anashukuru kwamba Mungu alimlinda, lakini bado anataka angekiri uasi wake kwa mama yake."
findings.translation_quote: Ingawa alitenda kwa ujinga, anashukuru kwamba Mungu alimtegemea, lakini bado anataka angekiri uasi wake kwa mama yake.

findings.location: <article> paragraph about stopping the bleeding (source.html): "after finding a little bandage and placing it on her cut"
findings.source_quote: The bleeding soon stopped, and after finding a little bandage and placing it on her cut, she quietly put her knife away and found a book to read.
findings.suggested_fix: "Bandage" must be translated correctly. Replace "banda" (which means 'shop' or is incorrect in this context) with "benda", "bandeji" or "kipande cha bandeji". Suggested Kiswahili: "Damu ilitoweka hivi karibuni, na baada ya kupata bandeji ndogo na kuiweka kwenye kata yake, alitulia kuweka kisu chake mbali..."
findings.translation_quote: Kuoterwa damu kwakatoweka hivi karibuni, na baada ya kupata banda ndogo na kuiweka kwenye kata yake, alitulia kuweka kisu chake mbali na kupata kitabu cha kusoma.

findings.location: <article> first figure img alt (source.html): alt of first image "A child whittling a stick with a small red-handled knife"
findings.source_quote: A child whittling a stick with a small red-handled knife
findings.suggested_fix: Translate "whittling" as "akichonga" (not "akitembea kifuniko"). Suggested alt text: "Mtoto akichonga kijiti kwa kisu kidogo chenye mkono mwekundu."
findings.translation_quote: Mtoto akitembea kifuniko cha kuni kwa kisu kidogo chenye mkono mwekundu

findings.location: <article> third paragraph (source.html): "It had a short, round handle..."
findings.source_quote: It had a short, round handle and he had inserted a small piece of steel into one end. He then honed the blade to a nice sharp edge.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the correct noun for "handle" (mshiko or mshituko) rather than "mshale" which reads as 'shaft'/'arrow'. Suggested Kiswahili: "Kilikuwa na mshiko mfupi, mviringo, na aling'ika kipande kidogo cha chuma mwishoni. Kisha akapiga msumari/akaisafisha kofia ya upanga hadi kuwa na ukingo mkali." (Keep sense clear and idiomatic.)
findings.translation_quote: Kilikuwa na mshale mfupi, mviringo na alikuwa ameweka kipande kidogo cha chuma mwishoni. Kisha alileta upanga hadi uke mkali.

findings.location: <article> paragraph about carving notches (source.html): "she had fun carving notches and shaving off small pieces of bark."
findings.source_quote: She still couldn’t make eyes and a nose appear, but she had fun carving notches and shaving off small pieces of bark.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer a natural Kiswahili rendering for "carving notches" and "bark"; avoid leaving English loanword "notchi" and use e.g. "kutengeneza mikunjo" or "kukata viganja" and "ganda la mti" for bark. Example: "Bado hakuweza kutengeneza macho na pua, lakini alifurahia kukata vinyweo na kuvua vipande vidogo vya ganda la mti."
findings.translation_quote: Bado hakuweza kutengeneza macho na pua kuonekana, lakini alikuwa anafurahia kukandia notchi na kukata vipande vidogo vya barki.
